title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck characterises the hyperbolic connected Riemann surfaces, meaning those not isomorphic to P^1, C, C^* or a complex torus. This page is page (2), the continuation for non-orientable 'surfaces conformes' (Klein surfaces, i.e. dianalytic structures). A non-orientable conformal surface X has an orientation double cover X^an, which is a Riemann surface carrying a fixed-point-free antiholomorphic involution. X is hyperbolic exactly when X^an is. So the non-hyperbolic non-orientable surfaces are the quotients of P^1, C, C^* and tori by free antiholomorphic involutions.

- P^1: the only free antiholomorphic involution up to conjugacy is the antipodal map, giving RP^2 = sphere/antipody.
- C: every antiholomorphic involution z -> a z̄ + b fixes a line, so C contributes nothing.
- C^*: z -> -1/z̄ is free, giving the open Möbius band, i.e. RP^2 minus a point.
- Tori: a torus with a free antiholomorphic involution is E(C) for a real smooth geometrically connected genus-1 curve E with E(R) = ∅. Grothendieck corrects 'elliptiques' to 'lisses, géom. connexes de genre 1', because such E has no real point and so is not an elliptic curve over R. The quotient X = E(C)/conj is a conformal Klein bottle. He states that up to isomorphism these E form a one-parameter family E^!_a, a in R_{>0}, presumably defined on an earlier page.

This completes the list of exceptional, non-hyperbolic conformal surfaces without boundary, orientable or not.

The second part opens the question of a canonical Riemannian metric on a conformal surface, starting with the boundaryless case. In the hyperbolic case there is a canonical metric of constant curvature -1, obtained by descent from the Poincaré metric on the universal cover H. Descent works because all automorphisms of H, including antiholomorphic ones in the non-orientable case, are isometries. The next page treats the flat cases:
- tori and Klein bottles: translation-invariant flat metric normalised to total area 1;
- C^* and RP^2 minus a point: flat metric, canonical only up to a positive scalar.

The purpose is a canonical metric framework for 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes', i.e. cutting and gluing conformal surfaces.
errors: Grothendieck writes that the universal covers of RP^2 and of RP^2 minus a point are respectively P^1_C and G_m,C. The universal cover of RP^2 minus a point (an open Möbius band) is simply connected, hence ≅ C, not C^*. C^* is its orientation double cover. The next page indeed works with X^an ≅ C^* and X̃ ≅ C, so 'rev. universels' should read 'revêtements d'orientation' (or X^an) for the second surface.

The list of exceptional non-orientable surfaces is correct and complete for surfaces without boundary: RP^2, open Möbius band, Klein bottles. The page does not justify why C contributes nothing (every antiholomorphic involution of C has a fixed line); this is a minor gap only.

ideas.what: Classification of non-hyperbolic non-orientable conformal (dianalytic) surfaces: RP^2, RP^2 minus a point, and Klein bottles E(C)/conj with E a real genus-1 curve without real points.
ideas.modern_name: Uniformisation of Klein surfaces / real algebraic curves; exceptional Klein surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein); systematised by Alling–Greenleaf (1971) and others in Klein surface theory

ideas.what: Insistence that real genus-1 curves with E(R)=∅ are 'lisses, géométriquement connexes de genre 1' rather than elliptic curves (no rational point); a one-real-parameter moduli family E^!_a, a>0.
ideas.modern_name: Real torsors under elliptic curves / real genus-one curves without real points; moduli of Klein bottles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical real algebraic geometry (Weichold, Gross–Harris 1981 for real curves)

ideas.what: Canonical Riemannian metric on a conformal surface: constant curvature -1 by descent from H in the hyperbolic case; flat area-normalised metric for tori and Klein bottles; flat metric up to scalar for C^* and the Möbius band.
ideas.modern_name: Uniformisation theorem / Poincaré metric; canonical metrics
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses canonical hyperbolic and flat structures for surgery / 'géométrie hyperbolique' and Teichmüller towers only in general terms.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, careful extension of uniformisation to non-orientable conformal surfaces, plus the classical canonical-metric setup. It is interesting only as documenting Grothendieck's preparation for surface surgery in the Esquisse period. It contains no new result or unexplored connection.
transcription_corrections: '(≃ Sphère conforme/antipodie)': the image reads 'Sphère conforme/antipodie' and the transcription is fine.
'≃ G_{m,C}[?]': the image shows '≃ G_m C' (G_{m,C}) without ambiguity; the [?] can be dropped (mathematically this should be the orientation double cover, not the universal cover).
'E^!_a': the superscript is hard to read and may be a prime, E'_a, referring to a family defined earlier.
'en prenant [-ECC-]': the struck-out text looks like 'E(C)' begun and cancelled.
